take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only for different access, dialect or stance, and ask 'could one prompt do this?' before approving anything bigger.
The failures happen at the handoffs, where a number gets dropped or a source gets rewritten. And nothing in the course checks whether the final briefing is true.
Ask what the agent can reach, and keep risky steps at 'propose' with a human approving.

monday.move: Ask IT what the approval process would be for an agent reading finance data. Then give the controller one month-end variance commentary to try with a single agent, in a read-only folder, no multi-agent setup.
monday.who: Me to IT, then my controller
monday.when: Ask Monday, controller trial after IT answers, likely 2-3 weeks
monday.stop_condition: Stop if the commentary needs more correcting than writing it fresh, or if IT says no on finance data.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data. Also, I still have no per-month cost figure.

misconception.why: I still lean on 'a licence you buy'. But I saw that agent setups need design, shared files, handoff checks and maintained rules, and the one-prompt test showed that results depend on how it's built. Nobody gave a price, so I haven't fully let go of the licence view.

one_line: Good rule on when not to use several agents and honest about its limits. But there was no cost number, and I left with an answer nobody had verified.
